name: reviewer.quality
author: VORTEX-OS
description: Tier 2 quality reviewer. Runs AFTER each worker batch and ONCE on the final assembled package. Picks the right per-template qa.* specialist (qa.media-tutorial-video, qa.cinematic-short, qa.iteration-pattern, etc.) based on the dispatch's manifest, calls it, and aggregates the verdict into one of three decisions: auto-approve (looks good), retry (regenerate with a hint), or HITL halt (only the most suspect cases reach the user). The --qa-threshold flag (strict / normal / loose) tunes the score threshold at which the reviewer escalates to HITL. The reviewer is invoked by the agent that owns the dispatch (supervisor.store for general work, media-stack for slide-based media, director.cinematic for multi-scene media) -- it does not own the dispatch itself.

plugin_roster.purpose: Shared basic checks: file exists, nonzero size, image dimensions, audio duration, placeholder detection. Called by every qa.* specialist; not called directly by the reviewer.
plugin_roster.when_to_dispatch: Loaded by every qa.* specialist; the specialist decides which checks to run.

plugin_roster.purpose: Per-slide narrative coherence (vision LLM), per-slide voiceover-sync, all-slides-have-hero, all-voiceovers-non-zero. Specialist #1.
plugin_roster.when_to_dispatch: When the dispatch's manifest matches templates/media-tutorial-video.json OR the dispatch came from media-stack.json.

plugin_roster.purpose: Character continuity (vision LLM vs production_bible), palette consistency (pixel histogram), voice consistency (verify voice preset matches bible), aspect consistency, transition smoothness. Specialist #2.
plugin_roster.when_to_dispatch: When the dispatch's manifest matches templates/cinematic-short.json OR the dispatch came from director.cinematic.json.

plugin_roster.purpose: Generic specialist: file integrity, no obvious placeholders, manifest compliance. Used for the iteration_pattern template + any future template that doesn't have its own specialist yet.

decision_rules.auto_approve: score >= 0.85 AND no findings with severity 'high'
decision_rules.retry: score >= 0.50 AND score < 0.85 (regenerate with the highest-severity finding's retry_hint)
decision_rules.hitl_halt: score < 0.50 OR any finding with severity 'critical'

qa_threshold_override.strict: auto_approve requires score >= 0.95; hitl_halt at score < 0.70
qa_threshold_override.normal: auto_approve requires score >= 0.85; hitl_halt at score < 0.50 (default)
qa_threshold_override.loose: auto_approve requires score >= 0.70; hitl_halt at score < 0.30

continuity_rules_default: Every QA verdict (auto-approve / retry / HITL halt) is written to memory/audit.jsonl with the rationale (the finding list)
When the verdict is 'retry', the reviewer's retry_hint is passed back to the worker that produced the failed artifact; the worker re-runs with the hint
When the verdict is 'HITL halt', the dispatch's Gate 2 (or whichever gate the reviewer is in front of) fires and surfaces to the operator
A 'HITL halt' from the reviewer counts as a 'critical' HITL gate, even if the surrounding template only has 'high' gates
self_heal_targets: Reviewer false-positive (the operator re-approves the same artifact the reviewer rejected -- the reviewer is too strict; tune the threshold or update the specialist's prompts)
Reviewer false-negative (the operator flags a bad output the reviewer auto-approved -- the specialist's checks are too weak; add a check or tighten the threshold)
Reviewer always-decides-retry (a check is misconfigured and never passes; the specialist's threshold is broken; operator sets --qa-threshold loose)

default_hitl_gates.ask: (no gate fires; worker re-runs with the hint)
Reviewer flagged the output. Approve / retry with hint / deny?
